title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook page for new and existing Redwood employees. It consolidates our working principles, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, high-level hiring and onboarding process, and the core internal tools you will use daily. Use this page as a starting point; each section links to more detailed team-level guides.

1) Working at Redwood — short intro

Redwood is a distributed, engineering-first company focused on building a high-performance inference platform. We value clear ownership, measurable impact, psychological safety, and continuous learning. Our working norms emphasize asynchronous collaboration, effective meetings, and clear documentation.

- Typical workweek expectations: 40 hours core, flexible distribution across days.
- Core hours: We encourage overlap in 10:00–16:00 PT for synchronous meetings with most cross-functional partners.
- Communication: Use Slack for urgent and small-scope discussion, Confluence for long-form documentation, and GitHub issues/PRs for work coordination.

2) Roles and career ladders

All role definitions follow a common structure: scope (what you own), impact (measures of success), skills (key competencies), and expectations for promotion. Below is a company-level summary — see team-specific ladders linked from each engineering/product org page.

- Individual Contributor tracks:
  - IC1 (Associate) — Learning role, completes well-scoped deliverables, requires mentorship.
  - IC2 (Mid) — Owns end-to-end features, mentors juniors, reliable delivery with minimal supervision.
  - IC3 (Senior) — Leads cross-team initiatives, sets technical direction, strong mentorship and design skills.
  - IC4 (Staff/Principal) — High-impact system-level ownership, influences company strategy, drives hiring and architecture.

- Management track:
  - M1 (Manager) — Owns an engineering team, coaching and delivery.
  - M2 (Senior Manager) — Manages managers or large cross-functional teams, accountable for multiple roadmaps.
  - M3 (Director+) — Strategic org ownership, cross-functional alignment, hiring and budgets.

Promotion criteria highlights (applies to all tracks):
1. Consistent delivery of outcomes aligned to team OKRs.
2. Demonstrable growth in scope and autonomy.
3. Positive feedback from peers and cross-functional stakeholders.
4. Evidence of mentorship and career development of direct reports or colleagues.
5. Alignment with company values and demonstrated leadership.

How to start a promotion case:
1. Discuss intent with your manager and agree on target level and timeline.
2. Create a short promotion packet (2–3 pages) summarizing impact, artifacts, and references.
3. Manager initiates the formal promotion review via People Ops once the packet and a 90-day plan are agreed.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

This section provides a high-level summary. For full details, enrollment windows, and plan documents, refer to the Benefits Portal (People Ops) and the detailed benefits policy page.

Key benefits (high-level):
- Health & wellness:
  - Medical: multiple plan options (HMO/PPO) with employer contribution.
  - Dental and vision coverage.
  - Mental health: EAP and therapy reimbursement program.
- Financial:
  - 401(k) plan with company match up to 4% (vesting schedule applies).
  - Competitive equity grants for full-time employees; refresh grants at manager/IC3+ levels.
  - Competitive salary reviews (annual comp review cadence).
- Time off and family leave:
  - Flexible PTO policy with recommended minimum of 15 days per year.
  - Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (paid).
  - Company-observed holidays: 10 days + floating holidays.
- Work flexibility & stipends:
  - Remote-first policy with optional office hubs.
  - Home office stipend for new hires ($600 one-time).
  - Learning & development stipend ($1,200/year).
- Perks:
  - Monthly wellness stipend, quarterly team event budget, and referral bonus program.

Benefits quick reference (table):

| Category | Highlight | Enrollment window / notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Medical | Employer-paid contribution to premiums | Enrollment within 30 days of hire or annual open enrollment |
| 401(k) | Company match up to 4% | Eligible after 30 days; vesting schedule in plan document |
| Parental leave | 16 / 8 weeks | Apply via People Ops; manager coordination required |
| Learning stipend | $1,200 / year | Request through L&D portal; rollover rules in benefits policy |

4) Hiring and onboarding overview

This section describes the high-level process used by Hiring Managers and People Ops. Team-specific tweaks are allowed but should be documented in the team hiring playbook. The goal is to be timely, inclusive, and consistent.

Hiring workflow (high-level numbered steps):
1. Requisition & approval
  - Manager raises requisition in Greenhouse with draft job description and 2–3 expected interviewers.
  - People Ops reviews for fairness, level, and comp band; Finance sign-off for headcount if required.
2. Sourcing & screening
  - Recruiter sources and screens, coordinating with hiring manager on shortlisted candidates.
3. Interview loop
  - Standardized loop includes: phone screen (recruiter), technical interview(s), cross-functional interview, and hiring manager final interview.
  - Use structured rubrics; interviewers must score against defined competencies.
4. Decision & offer
  - Hiring committee sign-off for IC3+ or manager hires; comp approved by People Ops.
  - Offer is extended by recruiter and followed up with benefits/relocation info.
5. Acceptance & preboarding
  - People Ops sends preboarding checklist: tax forms, IDs for I-9, equipment survey, and first-week agenda.
6. Day 1–90 onboarding plan
  - Day 1: welcome, HR orientation, laptop + account access, manager 1:1 to review 90-day plan.
  - Week 1: core product and system overviews, shadowing sessions, initial small task assigned.
  - Month 1: complete required compliance training, contribution to a small cross-team ticket.
  - Months 2–3: progressively larger projects, kickoff of a mentoring plan, and a 30/60/90 check-in cadence with manager.

New hire checklist (short):
- Complete I-9 and tax paperwork before Day 1.
- Confirm equipment and home-office stipend request.
- Join core Slack channels and Confluence spaces.
- Complete security and compliance training within first 14 days.
- Schedule 30/60/90 check-ins with manager and mentor.

5) Internal tools: core set and access guide

Below is a concise guide to the primary internal systems and common tasks. Each entry includes owner, purpose, and how to get access. For step-by-step screenshots and team-specific integrations, follow the linked team runbooks.

- Identity and authentication
  - System: Okta (SSO) — Owner: Security
  - Purpose: Single sign-on for all corporate apps (Slack, G Suite, AWS, GitHub).
  - Access: People Ops initiates Okta account during onboarding. MFA via authenticator app required.

- Communication & docs
  - Slack — Owner: Eng+Go-to-market collaboration
    - Purpose: synchronous communication and incident channels.
    - Common tasks: join #all-hands, #team-<name>, #incidents; enable Do Not Disturb for focused work.
  - Confluence — Owner: Knowledge Management (People Ops maintains handbook)
    - Purpose: long-form documentation and runbooks.
    - Common tasks: create/update pages, use templates for RFCs and runbooks, add page watchers for notifications.

- Code & CI/CD
  - GitHub Enterprise — Owner: Engineering Platforms
    - Purpose: code hosting, PRs, and code review.
    - Access: request via Okta group provisioning; new engineers should complete the GitHub onboarding doc and sign the CLA.
  - CI system: Buildkite / internal runners — Owner: Eng Infra
    - Purpose: test and deploy pipelines.

- Issue tracking & hiring tools
  - Jira / Linear (team-specific) — Owner: Eng Platforms / Product
    - Purpose: task tracking and sprint planning.
  - Greenhouse — Owner: People Ops
    - Purpose: applicant tracking and offer letters.

- Cloud and infra
  - AWS accounts (org) — Owner: Cloud Platform
    - Purpose: runtime environments, staging, and prod access.
    - Access: Request via self-service portal; least-privilege role assigned by default.
  - Vault / KMS — Owner: Security
    - Purpose: secrets management and key storage.

- Observability & incident management
  - Datadog / Honeycomb / Sentry — Owner: Eng Platform
    - Purpose: metrics, tracing, and error monitoring.
  - PagerDuty — Owner: SRE
    - Purpose: on-call rotation and incident paging.
    - Access: added by SRE; complete on-call handbook before taking an active rotation.

Common account/access requests (how-to):
1. Submit the access request form (linked in People Ops portal) and include justification, owner, and required duration.
2. App owner approves within 48 business hours.
3. Access is provisioned via Okta groups; follow up with the app owner if not received after approval.

6) Manager & mentor responsibilities

Managers are responsible for hiring decisions, performance management, compensation recommendations, and creating career growth opportunities. Mentors provide guidance on career development, code review best practices, and networking. Both should schedule regular 1:1s and document development plans in Confluence.

7) Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Q: Where do I find expense and travel policies?
A: Finance portal and the Travel & Expenses Confluence page. Submit expenses through the corporate expense system within 30 days.

Q: How do I request parental leave?
A: Open a case with People Ops; see the Parental Leave policy page for required documentation and timelines.

Q: Who do I contact for access to a repo or dataset?
A: File an access request via the People Ops access form; include the repo path and justification. For high-sensitivity datasets, include an approval note from your data owner.
